sprint_name: Feature Views Part 2 (Events, Fleet, CFN Loop)
reasoning: A* search analysis indicates PROCEED is optimal path despite 0.835 consensus (0.065 below 0.90 threshold). While functional work is high quality (1,237 LOC production code for 3 views complete), critical blockers prevent production deployment: (1) Memory leak in WebSocket hook (P0 - causes OOM crash), (2) Test execution blocked by WebSocket mock hangs (P0 - cannot validate ≥80% coverage requirement), (3) Chart.js 75% incomplete (P0 - only Pie chart implemented). These are IN-SCOPE technical blockers with clear remediation paths. Cost analysis: PROCEED (70) vs DEFER (20) vs ESCALATE (100). PROCEED selected because blockers are fixable within scope, team has demonstrated capability (1,238 LOC + 630 LOC fixtures), and targeted fixes avoid scope creep.

optimal_path.rationale: All blockers are in-scope technical issues with clear remediation paths. Memory leak fix (1h), test execution unblock (2-3h), Chart.js completion (6-8h) = 9-12 hours total. Targeted specialist agents (memory-safety, test-infrastructure, frontend-charts) address specific gaps without scope expansion.

alternative_paths.rejected_reason: Cannot ship with P0 memory leak (OOM crash) and zero test coverage validation. Standard mode requires production-ready code. DEFER would violate ≥80% coverage requirement and leave critical stability risk. Technical debt would compound into Sprint 3.4.

No scope ambiguity exists. All blockers are well-understood in-scope technical issues with clear fixes. Team has demonstrated capability in Sprint 3.1 (consensus 0.93) and 3.2 (consensus 0.89). Human escalation unnecessary and breaks CFN Loop autonomous decision-making principle.

defer_detail.production_readiness: NOT READY (P0 memory leak, zero coverage validation)

cost_analysis.optimization_rationale: PROCEED achieves production readiness and meets ≥80% coverage requirement at reasonable cost (70). DEFER saves 50 cost units but creates unacceptable technical debt (P0 memory leak persists, coverage requirement unmet). Risk-adjusted value: PROCEED delivers 100% business value at 3.5x cost vs DEFER 30% value at 1x cost. Value per cost: PROCEED (1.43) > DEFER (1.50) when accounting for debt remediation in Sprint 3.4.

consensus_assessment.rejection_rationale: Consensus gap of 7.3% is acceptable in magnitude BUT critical P0 blockers prevent production deployment. Standard mode allows DEFER for gaps ≤10% ONLY when no critical security/compilation/stability errors exist. Memory leak (OOM crash after 20+ route changes) is P0 stability blocker. Zero test coverage validation blocks ≥80% requirement verification. Cannot approve partial work with critical blockers.
